prompts.display_text: Pin Chimney Rock, the Nebraska landmark on the pioneer trail.
prompts.text_original: Drop a pin on Chimney Rock in western Nebraska, the spire the pioneers watched for days as they followed the North Platte River.
prompts.citation: Church History Topics, Pioneer Trek; Wikipedia and OpenStreetMap for the location, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: Chimney Rock is a tall rock spire rising above the North Platte River valley in western Nebraska. It was the most noted landmark in emigrant journals and could be seen for days as companies walked toward it. Latter-day Saint companies passed it on the north side of the river on the way to Fort Laramie.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country that received its first temple under President Spencer W. Kimball.
prompts.text_original: A country whose first temple was dedicated while Spencer W. Kimball was Church president (December 1973 to November 1985).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronology and ChurchofJesusChrist.org temple list, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: President Kimball served from December 1973 until his death on 5 November 1985. His years brought the first temples in South America (São Paulo, 1978), Asia (Tokyo, 1980) and Africa (Johannesburg, 1985), plus the Pacific and Mexico. Seoul Korea does not count: it was dedicated in December 1985, after he died.

answers.name: Brazil
answers.fact: São Paulo Brazil, dedicated 30 October–2 November 1978.

prompts.display_text: Pin a non-US country that has dedicated new temples in three or more different decades.
prompts.text_original: A country outside the United States where new temples were dedicated in at least three different decades.
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronology and ChurchofJesusChrist.org temple list, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: Nine countries outside the US have dedicated temples across three or more decades. Canada and Mexico span five decades each. Brazil and Japan span four, and Argentina, Chile, Peru, Guatemala and the Philippines three, usually the 1980s, 2010s and 2020s.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country whose own convert was called to preside over a mission there before 1880.
prompts.text_original: A country where one of its own converts was called to preside over a mission before 1880.
prompts.citation: Global Histories (churchofjesuschrist.org), country chronologies and overviews, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: Most early missions were led by Americans, but before 1880 several lands saw a local convert take charge: Dan Jones in Wales (1845), Carl Widerborg, a Swede, over Scandinavia (1858), Louis Bertrand in France (1859), Karl G. Maeser over the Swiss and German Mission (1868), and native presidents in Norway (1870), the Netherlands (1871) and Denmark (1873).

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: Karl G. Maeser, a convert from Dresden, was appointed president of the Swiss and German Mission on June 12, 1868.

answers.name: Denmark
answers.fact: In 1873 Christian Gries Larsen became the first Dane called to preside over the Scandinavian Mission.

answers.name: France
answers.fact: Louis Bertrand, baptized in Paris in 1850, was called in 1859 to reopen and preside over the French Mission.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: Welsh convert Dan Jones was appointed president of the Church in Wales in December 1845 and called again to preside in 1854.

answers.name: Netherlands
answers.fact: Sieberen van Dijk, the first native Netherlander to preside over the Netherlands Mission, was called in 1871.

answers.name: Norway
answers.fact: In 1870 the first native of Norway was called to preside over the Scandinavian Mission.

answers.name: Sweden
answers.fact: In 1858 Carl Widerborg, a Swede, became president of the Scandinavian Mission.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country whose first branch of the Church was organized during the 1850s.
prompts.text_original: A country whose first branch of the Church was organized in the 1850s.
prompts.citation: Global Histories (churchofjesuschrist.org), country chronologies and overviews, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: The 1850s were the decade of first branches. Missions opened across Europe, Africa, Asia and the Pacific, and converts were gathered into branches from Copenhagen (1850) to Karori, New Zealand (1855).

answers.name: Denmark
answers.fact: The Copenhagen Branch, the first in Denmark, was organized on September 15, 1850.

answers.name: France
answers.fact: William Howells organized the first branch in France at Boulogne-sur-Mer in 1850.

answers.name: Norway
answers.fact: The first branch in Norway was created at Risor on July 16, 1852, with 18 members.

answers.name: Sweden
answers.fact: Mikael Johnson organized the first branch in Sweden at Skonaback in 1853.

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: The Angrogna Branch, the first branch in present-day Italy, was organized in 1851.

answers.name: New Zealand
answers.fact: The Karori Branch became the first branch organized in New Zealand in April 1855.

answers.name: South Africa
answers.fact: The Mowbray Branch, the first branch in Africa, was organized on August 16, 1853.

answers.name: India
answers.fact: In 1851 a branch was organized in Calcutta after the first baptisms in India.

answers.name: Iceland
answers.fact: The first branch in Iceland was organized in the Westman Islands on June 19, 1853.
